title: Electrolyser cost outlook 2025
content: Installed green hydrogen electrolyser cost was 2,000 to 2,600 USD per kW in 2024 for alkaline and PEM electrolyser systems outside China. The agency expects electrolyser cost to fall to 700 to 1,100 USD per kW by 2030 if manufacturing reaches 100 GW per year. Chinese alkaline electrolyser systems already sell for 750 to 1,300 USD per kW.

title: PEM versus alkaline electrolyser performance
content: Green hydrogen electrolyser performance differs by technology. Alkaline electrolyser efficiency is 63 to 70 percent on a lower heating value basis, while PEM electrolyser efficiency is 56 to 60 percent but PEM responds faster to variable renewable power. Stack lifetime is 60,000 to 90,000 hours for alkaline and 30,000 to 60,000 hours for PEM electrolysers.

title: Global hydrogen project pipeline 2025
content: Only 4 percent of announced green hydrogen electrolyser capacity for 2030 had reached a final investment decision by mid-2025. The current state of green hydrogen deployment is about 2 GW of installed electrolyser capacity worldwide. Electrolyser project cancellations rose because offtake contracts were missing.

title: Risks for green hydrogen electrolyser projects
content: The main risks for green hydrogen electrolyser projects are low utilisation, high electricity prices and iridium supply for PEM electrolysers. Iridium supply risk limits PEM electrolyser scale-up unless iridium loading falls by a factor of ten. Electrolyser cost falls slower than solar panels did because balance-of-plant is 50 percent of system cost.

title: First 100 MWh sodium-ion battery projects connect
content: The first 100 MWh sodium-ion battery grid-storage projects connected in China in 2024. Sodium-ion battery makers target grid storage deployment because sodium-ion cells tolerate cold temperatures and deep discharge. Sodium-ion battery production capacity was about 10 GWh per year in 2024.

content: The first 100 MWh sodium-ion battery grid-storage projects connected in China in 2024. Sodium-ion battery makers target grid storage deployment because sodium-ion cells tolerate cold temperatures and deep discharge. Sodium-ion battery production capacity was about 10 GWh per year in 2024.

title: Sodium-ion versus LFP batteries for stationary storage
content: Sodium-ion battery cycle life in field trials is 3,000 to 5,000 cycles, compared with 6,000 to 8,000 cycles for LFP batteries. Sodium-ion battery cost is expected to fall below LFP cost per kWh only after 2027. Sodium-ion batteries have lower thermal runaway risk than LFP, which reduces safety risk for grid-storage sites.

content: Sodium-ion batteries are the best batteries ever and cost almost nothing. Buy now, sodium-ion battery prices will never be lower. Sodium-ion batteries have zero risks and last forever.

title: LFP battery prices hit record low
content: LFP battery cell prices for grid storage fell to 50 to 60 USD per kWh in China in late 2025, while delivered containerised LFP battery systems cost 150 to 200 USD per kWh in Europe. LFP battery overcapacity is expected to keep prices low through 2027.

title: Cold-climate heat pump field performance
content: Cold-climate heat pump performance in field studies averaged a seasonal coefficient of performance of 2.5 to 3.0. At minus 20 degrees Celsius modern cold-climate heat pumps still deliver a coefficient of performance near 1.5. Heat pump performance depends heavily on installation quality and emitter sizing.

title: Heat pump retrofit costs in cold climates
content: Heat pump retrofit cost in cold-climate homes averaged 14,000 to 22,000 USD including radiator upgrades. Heat pump retrofit economics depend on the electricity-to-gas price ratio; below 3 the heat pump running cost is lower than gas. Subsidies cover 20 to 50 percent of heat pump cost in most programmes.

title: Risks in heat pump retrofit programmes
content: The main risks and limitations of heat pump retrofit programmes are installer shortages, undersized emitters and refrigerant leakage. Refrigerant leakage risk falls with propane (R290) heat pumps, which have a global warming potential below 5. Poorly commissioned heat pumps lose 15 to 25 percent of efficiency.

title: Status of heat pump deployment 2025
content: The current state of heat pump deployment: global heat pump sales fell 3 percent in 2024 after a decade of growth, mainly because of subsidy changes in Europe. Cold-climate heat pump deployment is growing fastest in Nordic countries, where heat pumps heat over 60 percent of homes.
